cases.prompt: An enzyme assay shows a metal-dependent rate increase. Outline a control set that separates metal cofactor rescue from nonspecific ionic-strength or precipitation effects.

rubric.criterion: Uses metal-depleted/apo-enzyme and defined metal add-back
Includes a matched inert-salt or ionic-strength control
Checks soluble metal/enzyme or turbidity and includes activity blanks

limitations: This preserved three-criterion checklist is self-assessment, not an analytic grading rubric or an institutional grade.

cases.prompt: Redox project milestone 1 (suggested week 8). For the project's tokens A and B, select the cathode, reverse and scale the anode half-reaction, and write the balanced net reaction. Check both the electron count and the net charge.

rubric.criterion: I chose the cathode from the higher standard reduction potential.
I reversed only the anode half-reaction and scaled both so the electrons cancel.
I checked that token counts, electrons and net charge balance on both sides.
I checked my method on the open rehearsal before using the project tokens.

limitations: Optional self-check for the fictional redox-cell project. The response is saved privately and is never submitted, scored or graded; the separate inactive project draft and its proposed rubric remain unreviewed.

cases.prompt: Redox project milestone 2 (suggested week 8). Calculate E°cell, ΔG° = −nFE°cell and ln K = nFE°cell/(RT), and explain why a large K is consistent with the sign of ΔG°.

rubric.criterion: I used E°cell = E°(cathode) − E°(anode) without multiplying potentials by coefficients.
I used the n of the balanced net reaction in ΔG° and ln K.
I reported units and converted between J/mol and kJ/mol consistently.
I connected the signs of E°cell, ΔG° and ln K.

limitations: Optional self-check for the fictional redox-cell project. The response is saved privately and is never submitted, scored or graded; the separate inactive project draft and its proposed rubric remain unreviewed.

cases.prompt: Redox project milestone 3 (suggested week 8). Form the reaction quotient omitting pure solids, use the Nernst equation for the supplied activities, and compare the sign with the standard-state value.

rubric.criterion: I omitted pure solids and raised each activity to its stoichiometric coefficient.
I used E = E°cell − (RT/nF) ln Q with the same n as in milestone 2.
I explained why the potential rises or falls relative to E°cell for this Q.
I kept the activities as stipulated dimensionless values.

I divided the charge by F for moles of electrons and by n for the reaction extent.
I used the net-reaction coefficients for the amounts of A and B³⁺.
